title: SQLite join and aggregation
final_response:
Exported `/work/regional.csv` from a read-only connection (`file:billing.sqlite?mode=ro`), so the database was not modified — its md5 is identical before and after (`e077555c732eb71be89e5afdfc50bd9c`).

Query used:
```sql
SELECT c.region, SUM(i.amount_cents) AS total_cents, COUNT(i.id) AS invoice_count
FROM invoices i JOIN customers c ON c.id = i.customer_id
WHERE i.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY c.region
ORDER BY c.region ASC;
```

Result file contents:
```
region,total_cents,invoice_count
APAC,12500,2
EMEA,4000,1
```

Verification: re-computed the aggregation independently in Python and compared it line-by-line against the CSV — exact match (header + 2 rows). Notes on the data: 4 invoices total, 3 paid (the pending invoice #4 for customer B/EMEA, 9000 cents, is correctly excluded); every invoice matched a customer, so no rows were dropped by the inner join.
